episodes.177042: Another cold upper trough moved across central California on February 27 and 28 which resulted in another period of widespread precipitation across the area. The snow level was between 3000 and 4000 feet or much of this event which resulted in heavy snowfall for the  Sierra Nevada where several SNOTELs picked up an estimated 2 to 3 feet of new snowfall. Below the snow line, much of the San Joaquin Valley picked up between a quarter to a half inch of additional rainfall over already saturated soil while the Sierra foothills picked up between a half inch and an inch of combined liquid precipitation. Several roads in the mountains remained closed as a result of the continued snowfall across the area. The precipitation ended by the morning of March 1 as a colder and drier airmass pushed into central California.
episodes.177921: A severe line of thunderstorms, followed by high sustained wind gusts in the ridges, passed through the region on February 27th. ||Instability was limited by the time a cold front advanced through the region due to the time of the day, limited low level moisture, and earlier shower activity with the warm front. However low-level wind shear pushed convective storms to move at 60mph near I-70.  Wind gusts ranged between 40 to 55mph in portions of the Ohio River Valley.
episodes.177963: A few creeks and rivers reached minor flood stage over southeast WI after 1.5-2.0 inches of rain fell on a melting, shallow snowpack and frozen ground.

events.narrative: A 52mph wind gust was measured at Morgantown Airport at 803pm.
California Highway Patrol reported 2 large boulders in the west bound lane of SR 180 just to the northeast of Squaw Valley.

The Fox River near New Munster reached minor flood stage the morning of February 28th and continued until March 8th. Floodwaters surrounded a home at the intersection of Highway 50 and Highway W in the Town of Wheatland. Water was about 8 inches deep over 77th Street in the Town of Wheatland area. Water is in the backyards of some homes in the Village of Salem Lakes and Town of Wheatland areas.
